= CHERIoT memory subsystem: checker 3 (revocation engine) microarchitecture
:toc: left
:toclevels: 2
:sectnums:
:imagesdir: figures
:dft: ../out/fpv_revchk/draft

FPV checker 3 of `cheriot_mem_sys` checks the revocation engine: its sweep logic, TRVK
(tag revocation) filter and own tag filter, the sweep control with the status and epoch, the
`tbre_done` interrupt, the core write watch, the tag clear squash and the 2:1 tag arbiter. This
doc shows how each check of the checker 3 testplan, and checker 3's part of the
subsystem testplan, is done in the testbench; the testplan gives what each check
proves. The contracts and proof order are in the
xref:cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#revocation_checker[TB architecture], how the design works in the
xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc[design architecture], and the TL-UL rules in
the xref:../../tlul_abvip/tb_arch/tlul_abvip_uarch.adoc[TL-UL ABVIP]. Checker 1's
xref:cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch.adoc[uarch] is the pattern: the same layers, the same
TL-UL ABVIP and, for the engine's tag filter, the same tag filter model.

== Overview

=== Boundary

*Rule:* checker 3 holds the real revocation engine, from the register file's outputs to the
engine's three ports out (`tbre_tl_h`, the bitmap port, the 2:1 tag arbiter), with the tag clear
squash behind the arbiter. The testbench plays every block around it; the register file is a
blackbox whose outputs follow a model ([TB] decision D11; <<regfile_model>>).

.Checker 3: the real engine, the blocks the testbench plays, and the register file blackboxed

* *Plays the host:* the ABVIP assumes the host's TL-UL rules and asserts the device's. *Plays the
  device:* the reverse. *Checks both ends* (`CheckBoth`): assumes nothing, asserts every rule.
* `cored_tl_d` is a port whose two ends the testbench plays, the core and the cut tag filter: one
  ABVIP per end.
* 10 testpoints of the checker 3 testplan in five groups: start, status and interrupt (4), sweep
  (2), decision and clears (2), core write watch (1), errors (1); and checker 3's parts of
  `contracts`, `alert_causes`, `tlul_protocol` and `environment`. The register testpoints `csr`
  and `alert_test` are the CSR testing's ([TB] decision D11). `rev_end_to_end` has no property
  here: it follows from the checks of checkers 1 and 3.

*Ports inside the engine.* The spec places events inside the engine ([ToO] Revocation Engine: the
engine reads "through a TRVK filter of its own and a tag filter of its own"; "a socket merges its
downstream port with the engine's tag clears in front of the tag filter"), so the checker watches
four internal ports. The testplan's read port, clear port and windows are defined in its
Terms.

[cols="2,4,3",options="header"]
|===
|Port |What happens there |Testpoints that read it

|the engine's read port |the sweep logic presents its reads, in front of the TRVK filter; the
watch window starts here |`tbre_watch`, `tbre_decision`, `tbre_status`
|the TRVK downstream port |between the TRVK filter and the socket: the TRVK filter sees each
read's answer here, before it decides; W1's answer opens the lookup window |`tbre_decision`
|the engine's clear port |the sweep logic presents its clears, into the socket; the watch window
ends and the stale window starts here |`tbre_watch`, `tbre_decision`, `tbre_clear`
|the engine's tag filter's device port |the socket's output into the engine's tag filter: the
capability-load hint, and the tag filter checks |`tbre_sweep`, `tbre_clear`
|===

The engine's tag filter is the core's tag filter module without the WTRC and with tag-only writes:
its host port is `tbre_tl_h`, its meta port arbiter input 1. The bitmap port is the TRVK filter's
lookups of the revocation bitmap, to the engine's access checker.

'''

=== Testbench structure

*Rule:* the FPV top `revchk_env` holds `cheriot_mem_sys` with every input free. Two modules are
bound into the design: `revchk_env_rules`, with every assumption, and `revchk_checker`, with every
check and no assumption, so the same bind puts it into a simulation. Only the two binds and the
FPV top's port list name RTL nets.

.Checker 3's testbench: the FPV top holds the design; the assumptions and the checker are bound in
image::cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_revocation_uarch_figures.svg#fig2[Checker 3 testbench layers,align=center,width=900,height=665]

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Module |What it does

|`revchk_env` |the FPV top; after it, the bind of `revchk_env_rules`, formal only
|`revchk_env_rules` |the six played-port ABVIPs, the register file rules and the rules on top of
the ABVIPs (<<environment>>). Bound inside the design, it reaches the nets of the removed blocks
|`revchk_checker` |port events, the models, every check and cover (one banner section per testpoint), and the five `CheckBoth` ABVIPs on the links between real blocks: arbiter input 1 and
the engine's four internal ports
|`revchk_checker_bind` |binds the checker, in formal and in simulation
|`revchk_engine_model` |the engine model with the tracker (<<engine_model>>)
|`tfchk_model`, `tfchk_checker` |the tag filter model and the `tf_*` checks, shared with checker
1, with the filter's configuration as parameters (<<engine_tf>>)
|`revchk_pkg`, `tpchk_pkg` |the testplan's definitions as functions (<<definitions>>)
|===

* *Port events:* each port's handshake is decoded once, in the checker's port events section, into
  `req_vld` (a request presented), `req_fire` (taken), `rsp_vld` (an answer presented) and
  `rsp_fire` (taken). Eleven ports get them: `cored_tl_d`, the four internal ports, `tbre_tl_h`,
  the bitmap port, the two arbiter inputs, the arbiter output and the RMW filter upstream. The
  arbiter output's events use the RMW filter's `a_ready` and D channel, which the squash passes
  through unchanged.
* *The alert request* binds to the alert sender's own input, not to the OR the RTL drives it with,
  so `alert_causes` checks the wiring into the sender.
* *No port* reads the read port's tag answer or the clear's tag sideband: no check needs them. The
  clear's tag is checked where it leaves, at arbiter input 1.

[[environment]]
== Environment

*Rule:* every assumption of checker 3 sits in
link:{dft}/revchk_env_rules.sv[`revchk_env_rules.sv`]: a TL-UL ABVIP on each port the testbench
plays, holding TL-UL's own rules only, the register file rules, and this design's restrictions on
top, each naming its assumption ([DR] Assumptions) or contract ([TB] Contracts).

[[runs]]
=== Runs

[cols="1,5,4",options="header"]
|===
|Run |Checks |Rules beyond the common set

|safety A |contracts C3a, C3b, C11 and C21, which checker 1 assumes on arbiter input 1 |none of
checker 1's contracts: contracts C6 and C7 are left out
|V1 |every safety check of the testpoints |contracts C6, C7; the epoch counter starts at any value

|V3 |`tbre_errors` on malformed answers: _cause sets sweep error_, _error set next cycle_, _bad
answer raises fault_, _error only for a cause_, and its two malformed-answer cases |V1 without the
answer-shape rules `Rsp_Opcode` and `Rsp_Size` on `u_abvip_xbar` and `u_abvip_bitmap` ([TP] Run
variants)
|V4 |every V1 check |V1 with one mode switch, from any value to `MuBi4True`, while the engine is
idle and no start comes in that cycle: assumption A6 relaxed
|liveness A |contract C5, the bitmap answers taken |none
|liveness B |`tbre_done` _sweep ends_, and the engine's tag filter's two liveness checks
|assumption A10, contracts C1 and C2
|===

* The common set: the six ABVIPs, assumptions A6 and A12, contract C20 and the environment covers.
  Safety A proves what checker 1 assumes, so it may assume none of checker 1's contracts ([TB]
  Proof order).
* Run V3 only removes rules, so it adds behaviours: what run V1 proves stays proven. Run V4 adds
  the mode switch to every check of run V1.
* The checker is built once per run, with the define `REVCHK_RUN`; the Jasper script copies each
  run's checks into one task (<<jasper_setup>>).

|===
|Instance |Port, role |Parameters |Basis

|`u_abvip_core` |`cored_tl_d`, `PlayHost` |`MaxOutstanding` 2: at most two requests outstanding

halves"
|`u_abvip_core_tf` |`cored_tl_d`, `PlayDevice` |`MaxOutstanding` 2, list size only |the cut tag

|`u_abvip_m0` |arbiter input 0, `PlayHost` |`SrcW` 7: waiting requests differ in the low 7 bits of
`a_source` (assumption A9) |proven on the real port in checker 1
|`u_abvip_xbar` |`tbre_tl_h`, `PlayDevice` |defaults |`xbar_main` as a TL-UL device
|`u_abvip_bitmap` |bitmap port, `PlayDevice` |defaults |proven for the real access checker in

|`u_abvip_rmw` |RMW filter upstream, `PlayDevice` |defaults |proven on the real RMW filter in

|`u_abvip_m1` |arbiter input 1, `CheckBoth` |`SrcW` 7 |both ends real
|`u_abvip_rd`, `u_abvip_trvk` |read port, TRVK downstream port, `CheckBoth` |`MaxOutstanding` 2,
asserted: "Up to two words are in flight" ([ToO]) |both ends real
|`u_abvip_clr`, `u_abvip_tf` |clear port, tag filter device port, `CheckBoth` |defaults |both ends
real
|===

* *Two ABVIPs on `cored_tl_d`:* no role assumes both ends ([ABVIP] Roles). Each one's assertions
  follow from the other's assumptions, so they prove at once and check nothing; what matters is
  that both ends' rules are assumed.
* *The `CheckBoth` ABVIPs:* `u_abvip_m1` proves on arbiter input 1 the TL-UL rules checker 1
  assumes there (contract C21). On the four internal ports the engine model matches answers by
  source ([ToO]: each read "with a source ID of its own"), so their `Src_Unique` rule checks that
  matching back.
* Integrity is free on every port: a broken integrity is legal stimulus (`tbre_errors` needs it).
* Lists keep their default size until a proof is slow, as checker 1 does ([UA1] decision D22).

  word or tag. Reset is free mid-run.

[[regfile_model]]
=== Register file model

*Rule:* the register file is a blackbox; its outputs to the engine and the interrupt logic are
free, and three rules keep them to what the register file does by its spec ([TB] decision D11,
contract C20). Every other output stays free: software may write it in any cycle.

.The register file blackboxed: its outputs follow the model's rules; the engine's writes into it are watched
image::cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_revocation_uarch_figures.svg#fig3[Register file model,align=center,width=880,height=496]

[cols="1,3,4,3",options="header"]
|===
|Rule |Output to the engine |What it says |Basis

|R1 |`TBRE_BASE_ADDR`, `TBRE_NUM_CAPS` |change only after a cycle in which `TBRE_REGWEN` is 1
|[HJSON] `TBRE_REGWEN.en`: "locking `TBRE_BASE_ADDR`, `TBRE_NUM_CAPS` and `TBRE_START`{empty}"
|R2 |`TBRE_START` write strobe |only in a cycle in which `TBRE_REGWEN` is 1 |the same
|R3 |`INTR_STATE.tbre_done` |rises only in the cycle after the interrupt logic's set request
|[REGS] `INTR_STATE` is `rw1c`: hardware sets it, software clears it
|R4 |`INTR_ENABLE`, `INTR_TEST`, `ALERT_TEST` |free |[REGS] `rw`, `wo`
|===

* *Why "after a cycle" in rule R1:* a write accepted while `TBRE_REGWEN` is 1 changes the register
  from the next cycle. Rule R2's strobe belongs to the write's own cycle: `TBRE_START` is a `hwqe`
  register.
* *The status registers:* `TBRE_STATUS` is written by the engine only (`hwo`). The checks read the
  engine's set requests into it (the testplan's set request), and the engine model keeps the busy
  field as the engine last wrote it. `TBRE_REGWEN` and `TBRE_EPOCH` are `hwext`: the checks read
  what the engine drives.
* *What the register file returns to software,* and when it takes a request, is the CSR testing's
  ([TB] decision D11).
* *No rule beyond these:* each rule removes a behaviour the register file cannot show; another
  rule would be a data assumption. A simulation with the rules bound to the real register file
  checks contract C20 cheaply (simulation).

it expects, and its runs (<<runs>>). Each block shows its model first, then the testpoints that use

status, checker 3).

[[definitions]]
=== Definitions in `revchk_pkg`

*Rule:* each term of the testplan is one function, computed from the spec's numbers, never from
the RTL's. The address functions are checker 1's, in `tpchk_pkg`, which both checkers import.

[cols="2,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|Function |Testplan term |Source

|`is_main_sram`, `is_nvm`, `is_tagged`, `region_top` |in the main SRAM; in the NVM; in a tagged
region; its top |[IF] parameters
|`tag_word`, `tag_bit` |tag word, tag bit |[ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map; bit order: an open question
|`rev_word`, `rev_bit`, `is_revocable` |revocation word and bit; revocable base |[ToO] Meta SRAM
Address Map, `revbm` window; [PG]
|`cap_base` |base, in the four steps of the testplan |[ISA] §7.13.3, Sail `getCapBoundsBits`
|`is_sealing` |sealing capability |[ISA] CLC, Sail `isSealingCap`; no permissions: an open question
|`sweep_caps`, `in_sweep` |N, the swept capabilities |[ToO] Revocation Engine
|`is_taken_start` |taken start |[ToO] Revocation Engine
|`is_ena`, `is_intg_ok`, `is_malformed_read`, `is_failed_read` |CHERIoT mode; integrity ok;
malformed; lookup failed |[ToO] Access Checkers; [TLUL] Usage of User Bits; [TLPC]
|===

* *Integrity:* the integrity functions call `tlul_pkg`{empty}'s, the shared bus integrity code,
  out of scope here as in checker 1 ([UA1] Definitions).
* *The decode is the ISA's, never the RTL's:* the TRVK filter calls `ibex_cheriot_pkg` functions;
  the testbench decodes the base and the permissions itself ([TB] decision D13).

The worked example of this doc, computed from the testplan's terms:

[cols="3,5",options="header"]
|===
|What |Value

|the sweep |`BASE` `0x1000_1230`, `NUM` 2, so N is 2: the capabilities at `0x1000_1230` and
`0x1000_1238`
|the tracked capability |the second: `0x1000_1238`, W0 at `0x1000_1238`, W1 at `0x1000_123C`
|its tag in memory |tag word `0x1100_8C48`, tag bit 7; stored tag 1
|what memory holds |W0 `0x1000_4010` (the address), W1 `0x7E00_8000` (the metadata)
|W1 decoded |permissions `0x3F`: a read-write memory capability, not sealing; object type 0;
exponent 0; base field 0
|its base |`0x1000_4000`: in the main SRAM, so revocable
|its revocation word and bit |`0x1100_0100`, bit 0
|the bitmap word |`0x0000_00FF`: software freed the 64-byte object at `0x1000_4000`, bits 0 to 7
|the decision |revoked: the engine clears the tag, a write of tag 0 to word `0x1100_8C48`, bit 7
|===

[[engine_model]]
=== Engine model

*Rule:* the engine model follows the engine as [ToO] Revocation Engine describes it: it decodes
each start, keeps the sweep's range, follows one capability of the sweep through its reads, its
lookup, its decision, its clear and its windows, keeps the core's writes in flight, and flags the
error causes. It predicts what the engine must do; the properties compare. It drives no port. Its
parts sit under the blocks that read them: the sweep (<<sweep_part>>), the decision
(<<decision_part>>), the core write watch (<<watch_part>>), the error causes (<<causes_part>>).

==== What the model watches and predicts

.The engine model: what it watches, what it keeps, and which checks compare each prediction
image::cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_revocation_uarch_figures.svg#fig4["Engine model: what it watches, keeps and predicts",align=center,width=900,height=955]

[cols="1,4,3,8,4",options="header"]
|===
|Point |Watches |Sent by |The model keeps or predicts |Checked by

|(1) |a start: the `TBRE_START` strobe with `BASE` and `NUM` |register file model |the start's
kind, taken or ignored, `BASE` and N; the tracked capability |input
|(2) |the core's writes on `cored_tl_d` |`u_abvip_core`, `u_abvip_core_tf` |the writes in flight;
whether one touches the tracked capability |input
|(3) |the answers on `tbre_tl_h` |`u_abvip_xbar` |the tracked capability's words, their `d_error`
and integrity; error causes |input
|(4) |the bitmap answers; the answers to the engine's tag reads and clears |`u_abvip_bitmap`,
`u_abvip_rmw` |the tracked capability's bitmap word, whether its lookup failed; error causes |input
|(5) |the reads on the read port and `tbre_tl_h` |RTL engine |every read inside the sweep; both
words of the tracked capability before the sweep ends; at most two outstanding
|<<uw_tbre_sweep,`tbre_sweep`>>
|(6) |the lookups on the bitmap port |RTL TRVK filter |the tracked capability's lookup, of the
revocation word of its base, while the TRVK filter holds its W1 answer; none for a base outside
the main SRAM |<<uw_tbre_decision,`tbre_decision`>>
|(7) |the clears: at the clear port, at arbiter input 1, at the RMW filter |RTL engine, arbiter,
squash |a clear exactly for a revoked capability not touched in its watch window; a read at the
RMW filter after a touch in its stale window; held there until taken
|<<uw_tbre_decision,`tbre_decision`>>, <<uw_tbre_clear,`tbre_clear`>>,
<<uw_tbre_watch,`tbre_watch`>>
|(8) |the engine's writes into the status registers, `TBRE_REGWEN`, `TBRE_EPOCH`, the interrupt
|RTL sweep control |`TBRE_REGWEN` low from the cycle after a taken start until the tracked
capability is resolved; busy, active, epoch, `start_err`, `sweep_err` and the interrupt
|<<uw_tbre_start,`tbre_start`>>, <<uw_tbre_status,`tbre_status`>>,
<<uw_tbre_epoch,`tbre_epoch`>>, <<uw_tbre_intr,`tbre_intr`>>, <<uw_tbre_errors,`tbre_errors`>>
|(9) |the engine's fault inputs and the alert request |RTL engine, alert logic |a fault only after
an engine cause; the alert after one |<<uw_tbre_errors,`tbre_errors`>>,
<<uw_contracts,`contracts`>>, <<uw_alert_causes,`alert_causes`>>
|===

The model also watches the outputs (5) to (9): what the engine has done decides what is due next.
The engine's tag filter has its own model, checker 1's (<<engine_tf>>); the engine model reads
only the tag it returns with W0's answer, at the TRVK downstream port.

'''

==== What the model remembers

*Rule:* the model keeps the sweep, the core's writes in flight, the reads in flight through the
TRVK filter, and one tracked capability per sweep. The tracked capability is chosen at the taken
start by an index the tool may set to anything below N, so every swept capability is followed in
some trace; an index of N or more tracks nothing in that sweep.

[cols="4,4",options="header"]
|===
|The model remembers |Which checks use it

|the sweep: `BASE`, N, `TBRE_REGWEN` and the start of the cycle before |`tbre_start`,
`tbre_sweep` _Gets inside sweep_, `tbre_decision` _clear only if revoked_
|the status owed: the busy field, a `start_err` or `sweep_err` set request owed or due, a cause in
this sweep, an engine alert cause since reset |`tbre_start`, `tbre_status`, `tbre_epoch`,
`tbre_errors`, `contracts`
|the core's accepted, unanswered requests, at most two: capability and whether a write |the touch
(`tbre_watch`, `tbre_decision` _revoked gets cleared_)
|the reads in flight through the TRVK filter, at most two: word, source on each port, arrived,
looked up |`tbre_decision` _lookup is bitmap Get_ and _no lookup outside main SRAM_
|the tracked capability's words: read taken, source and answer per port; data, `d_error` and
integrity; its tag |`tbre_sweep` _both words read_, `tbre_decision`, `tbre_errors` _read error, no
clear_
|its lookup: taken, source, answered, bit set, failed |`tbre_decision`
|its clear: presented, taken, source, answered, arrived at the RMW filter; touched in its watch
and stale windows |`tbre_decision`, `tbre_clear`, `tbre_watch`, `tbre_status`
|===

*Which answer belongs to which request.* Reads and their answers are matched by `a_source`, which
TL-UL keeps unique while outstanding (the `CheckBoth` ABVIPs check it on the internal ports).
Clears are matched by address, inside the capability's 8 bytes at the clear port, and by tag word
and bit select on the meta path. Each word is followed on three ports: the read port, the TRVK
downstream port and `tbre_tl_h`; its data, `d_error` and integrity come from `tbre_tl_h`, its tag
from W0's answer at the TRVK filter.

*Tracking phases.* The phase is worked out each cycle from what has happened, not kept in a flop;
the testplan's case _each tracking phase_ covers each one.

[cols="2,5,4",options="header"]
|===
|Phase |The tracked capability |Ends when

|idle |none followed yet |a taken start with an index below N
|reading |W0 and W1 presented, taken and answered |W1's answer reaches the TRVK filter
|in lookup |the TRVK filter holds W1's answer; its lookup |W1's answer leaves on the read port
|decided |revoked or not is known; a clear is due or not |the clear is presented, or the
capability is resolved without one
|clearing |the clear on its way: arbiter input 1, the RMW filter, its answer |the clear's answer
at the clear port
|resolved |nothing new: the sweep may end |`TBRE_REGWEN` rises
|===

A lookup answer that comes after W1's answer left can make a capability revoked late, which moves
it from resolved back to decided; the checks read the events, not the phase.

.Example: the tracked capability `0x1000_1238`, revoked
[cols="1,5,5",options="header"]
|===
|Step |What happens |What the model expects

|1 |A start: `BASE` `0x1000_1230`, `NUM` 2, CHERIoT mode, `TBRE_REGWEN` 1. The tool picks the
second capability |a taken start: N is 2; `TBRE_REGWEN` 0 in the next cycle; the tracked
capability is `0x1000_1238`
|2 |The engine presents W0's read of `0x1000_1238` on its read port |a read inside the sweep; the
watch window starts
|3 |W0's `Get` is taken on `tbre_tl_h`, hinted at the tag filter |a full-word `Get`, hinted; at most
two reads outstanding
|4 |W0's answer: `0x1000_4010`, no error; its tag, 1, at the TRVK downstream port |nothing due; the
model keeps the data and tag 1
|5 |W1's read of `0x1000_123C`, presented and taken; its answer `0x7E00_8000` reaches the TRVK
filter |base `0x1000_4000`, not sealing, revocable: a lookup is due; the lookup window opens
|6 |The lookup: a `Get` of `0x1100_0100` on the bitmap port; the answer `0x0000_00FF`, no error
|this is the lookup of the revocation word of the base; bit 0 is set: revoked
|7 |W1's answer leaves on the read port |the lookup window closes; a clear is due
|8 |The clear: a write in the capability's 8 bytes, tag 0, on the clear port |no touch in the
watch window: the clear is allowed; the stale window starts
|9 |The clear leaves on arbiter input 1 |a write of tag 0 to word `0x1100_8C48`, bit 7, once
|10 |It reaches the RMW filter and is held there until taken |no touch in the stale window: a
write; unchanged until taken
|11 |The clear's answer at the clear port |resolved: `TBRE_REGWEN` may rise
|===

Steps 3 to 5 may overlap: up to two reads are in flight ([ToO]). A core write in
`0x1000_1238`-`0x1000_123F` between steps 2 and 8 means no clear at step 8; one between steps 8 and
10 means a read at step 10.

'''

=== Start, status and interrupt

*Rule:* the starts, `TBRE_REGWEN`, the busy field, `TBRE_EPOCH` and the interrupt are checked at
the engine's writes into the register file and at `intr_tbre_done_o`, against the model's sweep
([TP] Start, status and interrupt).

[[sweep_part]]
==== The sweep and the status owed

Part of the engine model (<<engine_model>>).

*Rule:* a start is taken or ignored by [ToO]'s three conditions; a taken start fixes `BASE` and N
for the sweep. The model also keeps what the engine owes the status registers.

[cols="2,4,4",options="header"]
|===
|What the model keeps |From |Used by

|start kind, this cycle |the `TBRE_START` strobe written 1, the mode, `NUM`, `BASE` in a tagged
region |`tbre_start`
|`BASE` and N of the sweep |the registers at the taken start |`tbre_sweep`; the tracker
|a `start_err` set request owed, one due |an ignored start, until its set request; due in the
cycle after |`tbre_start` _error only after ignored start_, _error set next cycle_
|an error cause in this sweep |any cause of <<causes_part>>, from the taken start until the
engine stops being active, that cycle included |`tbre_epoch` _steps unless error_
|the busy field |the engine's busy set requests |`tbre_status` _busy follows REGWEN_
|===

The owed and due flags are credits: each ignored start gives one, its set request uses it up. So a
second set request for one start, or one after a taken start, finds no credit.

'''

[[uw_tbre_start]]
==== tbre_start: which starts start a sweep

Testplan. A taken start makes the engine active; an ignored start moves
nothing and sets `start_err`, which nothing else sets.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Run

|_taken start activates_ (CHK_TBRE_START_01) |a taken start
|`TBRE_REGWEN` is 0 in the next cycle |V1, V4
|_REGWEN falls only on start_ (CHK_TBRE_START_02) |`TBRE_REGWEN`
falls |the cycle before was a taken start |V1, V4
|_ignored start changes nothing_ (CHK_TBRE_START_03) |an ignored
start |in the next cycle `TBRE_REGWEN` is 1, `TBRE_EPOCH` as before and the busy field 0 |V1, V4
|_ignored start sets error_ (CHK_TBRE_START_04) |an ignored start |a
`start_err` set request, at some point |V1, V4
|_error set next cycle_ (CHK_TBRE_START_05) |an ignored start |that
set request by the next cycle |V1, V4
|_error only after ignored start_ (CHK_TBRE_START_06) |a `start_err`
set request |an ignored start is owed one |V1, V4
|===

_taken start activates_ and `tbre_status` _REGWEN low after start_ are one property.

'''

[[uw_tbre_status]]
==== tbre_status: active, busy and the first read

Testplan. `TBRE_REGWEN` is low from the cycle after a taken start until
the sweep is resolved; busy follows it a cycle later, the epoch's active bit in the same cycle.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Run

|_REGWEN low after start_ (CHK_TBRE_STATUS_01) |a taken start
|`TBRE_REGWEN` is 0 in the next cycle |V1, V4
|_REGWEN rises only when resolved_ (CHK_TBRE_STATUS_02)
|`TBRE_REGWEN` rises |the tracked capability is resolved, and no read, lookup or clear of the
engine is outstanding |V1, V4
|_busy follows REGWEN_ (CHK_TBRE_STATUS_03) |every cycle |the busy
field, as the engine last wrote it, is the inverse of `TBRE_REGWEN` a cycle before |V1, V4
|_active follows REGWEN_ (CHK_TBRE_STATUS_04) |every cycle
|`TBRE_EPOCH.active` is the inverse of `TBRE_REGWEN` |V1, V4
|===

Resolved uses the meaning an open question proposes.

'''

[[uw_tbre_epoch]]
==== tbre_epoch: the epoch counts sweeps without an error

Testplan. The count steps by one in the cycle `active` falls after a
sweep without an error cause, and at no other time.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Run

|_steps unless error_ (CHK_TBRE_EPOCH_01) |`TBRE_EPOCH.active`
falls |the count is one more than before when the model saw no error cause in the sweep, else
unchanged |V1, V4
|_count stable otherwise_ (CHK_TBRE_EPOCH_02) |any other cycle |the
count is unchanged |V1, V4
|===

The counter starts at any value in runs V1 and V4, the same after every reset, so the wrap is reached
.

'''

[[uw_tbre_intr]]
==== tbre_intr: the interrupt

Testplan. `tbre_done` is set when a sweep ends or software tests it, and
only then; the interrupt line follows the enabled state.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Run

|_sweep end or test sets_ (CHK_TBRE_INTR_01) |`TBRE_REGWEN` rises, or
an `INTR_TEST` write of 1 |a set request for `INTR_STATE` in that cycle |V1, V4
|_set only on end or test_ (CHK_TBRE_INTR_02) |a set request |the
cycle is one of those |V1, V4
|_line follows state_ (CHK_TBRE_INTR_03) |every cycle
|`intr_tbre_done_o` equals `INTR_STATE` and `INTR_ENABLE` both set, of this cycle or of the cycle
before |V1, V4
|===

The draft property lets each cycle pick its own latency, so a one-cycle pulse can be lost without
a failure; the testplan's check holds one latency for the whole trace (open decisions).

'''

=== Sweep

*Rule:* every request on `tbre_tl_h` is checked against the model's sweep, and the tracked
capability's words against the tracker ([TP] Sweep). The model part is the tracked capability's
reads (<<engine_model>>).

[[uw_tbre_sweep]]
==== tbre_sweep: exactly the swept words are read

Testplan. A sweep reads exactly the words of the swept capabilities,
full-word `Get`{empty}s with the hint and a valid integrity, at most two at a time.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Run

|_sweep read carries valid integrity_ (CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_01) |a read is
presented on `tbre_tl_h` |a valid command integrity |not built
|_both words read_ (CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_02) |`TBRE_REGWEN` rises |both
words of the tracked capability had a full-word `Get` taken on `tbre_tl_h` |V1, V4
|_Gets inside sweep_ (CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_03) |a request is presented on
`tbre_tl_h` |a full-word `Get` of a swept capability's word, while active |V1, V4
|_at most two outstanding_ (CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_04) |every cycle |at most
two reads outstanding on `tbre_tl_h`; their `a_source` differ (ABVIP rule TL08 on `u_abvip_xbar`)
|V1, V4
|_Gets carry hint_ (CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_05) |a `Get` is presented at the
engine's tag filter's device port |its tag sideband, the hint, is 1 |V1, V4
|===

_sweep read carries valid integrity_ has no property in the draft yet (open decisions).

'''

[[uw_tbre_done]]
==== tbre_done: every sweep ends

Testplan. Every sweep ends, given `xbar_main`, the bitmap port and the RMW
filter answer.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Run

|_sweep ends_ (CHK_TBRE_DONE_01) |a taken start |`TBRE_REGWEN` is 1
again, at some point |liveness B
|===

The clears pass the real 2:1 tag arbiter, so the sweep ends only if the arbiter never starves
input 1: an open question.

'''

=== Decision and clears

*Rule:* each lookup is checked at the bitmap port against the reads the TRVK filter holds, each
clear at the clear port and arbiter input 1 against the model's decision, and the engine's tag
filter against the shared tag filter model ([TP] Decision and clears).

[[decision_part]]
==== The decision

Part of the engine model (<<engine_model>>).

*Rule:* a swept capability is revoked when it is tagged, not a sealing capability, has a revocable
base, and its base's revocation bit is set or its lookup failed ([TP] Terms, Revoked). The model
decodes the base and the permissions from the words by the ISA's steps (<<definitions>>).

[cols="3,2,1,2,3",options="header"]
|===
|Capability (W0, W1) |Base |Tag |Sealing |Lookup, clear

|`0x1000_4010`, `0x7E00_8000` |`0x1000_4000` |1 |no |lookup of `0x1100_0100` bit 0; clear if set
|`0x1000_4010`, `0x0200_8000` (permissions 1: sealing, US) |`0x1000_4000` |1 |yes |no clear
|`0x3000_0400`, `0x7E00_8000` (an NVM pointer) |`0x3000_0400` |1 |no |base not revocable: no
lookup, no clear
|`0x1000_4010`, `0x7E00_8000`, untagged |`0x1000_4000` |0 |no |no clear
|===

*Which lookup is the tracked capability's:* the spec says a capability "whose bitmap lookup fails"
is revoked, but not when the lookup happens. The model takes the first lookup presented while the
TRVK filter holds the capability's W1 answer: from W1's answer arriving at the TRVK downstream port
to its leaving on the read port. The TRVK filter needs W1 to decode the base, and it applies the
load barrier to W1's answer, so the lookup lies in that window (DV reading).

*Every lookup, not only the tracked one's:* the model follows every read in flight between
the read port and the TRVK downstream port, at most two, by its word. It then knows in every cycle
whether the TRVK filter holds a W1 answer that has had no lookup yet.

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Event |What the model's reads in flight do

|a read taken on the read port, or on the TRVK downstream port |the read's place, found by its
word, records that port's source; the first of the two ports makes it. The TRVK filter may forward
a read before its own port takes it
|an answer taken on the TRVK downstream port |the TRVK filter now holds that answer
|a lookup presented, in its first cycle |it belongs to the first held W1 answer without a lookup;
_lookup is bitmap Get_ fails if there is none
|an answer taken on the read port |the TRVK filter let the answer go: the place is freed
|===

_no lookup outside main SRAM_ judges a lookup as the tracked capability's only when the TRVK filter
holds no other W1 answer, so it never blames the tracked capability for another's lookup.

'''

[[uw_tbre_decision]]
==== tbre_decision: which capabilities are revoked

Testplan. A tagged, non-sealing capability with a revocable base gets
a lookup of its base's revocation word; a capability gets a clear exactly when it is revoked and no
core write touched it in its watch window.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Run

|_lookup carries valid integrity_ (CHK_TBRE_DECISION_01) |a lookup
is presented on the bitmap port |a valid command integrity |not built
|_lookup when needed_ (CHK_TBRE_DECISION_02) |the TRVK filter
holds the tracked capability's W1 answer, and the capability needs a lookup |a full-word `Get` of
the revocation word of its base, in that window |V1, V4
|_no lookup outside main SRAM_ (CHK_TBRE_DECISION_03) |a lookup is
presented while the TRVK filter holds the tracked capability's W1 answer, and no other |its base
is in the main SRAM |V1, V4
|_lookup is bitmap Get_ (CHK_TBRE_DECISION_04) |any lookup is
presented; every cycle |a full-word `Get` of a bitmap word, while the TRVK filter holds a W1 answer
with no lookup yet; the reads in flight fit the model's two places |V1, V4
|_revoked gets cleared_ (CHK_TBRE_DECISION_05) |`TBRE_REGWEN`
rises |if the tracked capability was read without error, is revoked and was not touched in its
watch window, its clear was presented |V1, V4
|_clear only if revoked_ (CHK_TBRE_DECISION_06) |a clear is
presented on the clear port |it is sent while active, inside a swept capability; for the tracked
one, the model has decided it and found it revoked |V1, V4
|===

* _lookup carries valid integrity_ has no property in the draft yet (open decisions).
* An untagged tracked capability is not checked by _clear only if revoked_: the testplan gives the
  untagged rows no rule.

'''

[[engine_tf]]
==== The engine's tag filter

*Rule:* the engine's tag filter is checked against checker 1's tag filter model
([UA1] Tag filter model), bound to this second instance with its configuration: no WTRC, tag-only
writes. Both checkers use the same two modules in
link:{dft}/tag_filter/[`tag_filter/`], each instance with its own parameters.

[cols="2,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|Port of the engine's tag filter |Here |For the core's, in checker 1

|device port |the socket's output, driven by the real engine |`cored_tl_d`, driven by
`u_abvip_core`
|host port |`tbre_tl_h`, answers from `u_abvip_xbar` |`cored_tl_h`, answers from `u_abvip_xbar`
|meta port |arbiter input 1, answers through the arbiter from `u_abvip_rmw` |arbiter input 0
|===

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Parameter |For the engine's tag filter

|`NvmCapStores` 0 |no WTRC ([ToO] WTRC: "the revocation engine's tag filter has no WTRC"): a tagged
write to the NVM is a plain write, with its lookup
|`TagOnlyWrites` 1 |a write makes one meta request and no host request, and is answered once with
the meta answer's `d_error` (`REQ_TBRE_23a`; DV reading). So `tf_forward` expects no
host request for a write, its answer has only the meta answer as a part, and its error is the meta
answer's; every other check reads the same
|`CoverCases` 0 |the testplan's `tf_*` cases run on the core's filter only
|`RunLive` |liveness B adds `tf_flow` _request eventually accepted_ and _request eventually
answered_
|===

* *Only the engine's traffic reaches it:* hinted full-word reads in pairs and tag clears. The
  model's other cases stay unreached here, which is no gap: checker 1 reaches them on the core's
  instance.
* The shared checker passes the model's predictions to its parent; checker 3's covers read the
  oldest open request, its meta error and the captured tag, to reach their cases.

'''

[[uw_tbre_clear]]
==== tbre_clear: the clear and the engine's tag filter

Testplan. A clear is one tag write of tag 0 to the capability's tag word
and bit, on arbiter input 1, once per sweep; the engine's tag filter keeps the tag filter rules.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Run

|_clears tracked bit once_ (CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_01) |the tracked
capability's clear leaves on arbiter input 1 |a write of tag 0 to its tag word, with its tag bit;
no second clear of it in this sweep |V1, V4
|_writes tag 0_ (CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_02) |any write is presented on
arbiter input 1 |its tag is 0 |V1, V4
|_tag filter checks hold_ (CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_03) |as each check of the
checker 1 tag filter testpoints |the `tf_*` checks, on the engine's tag
filter (<<engine_tf>>) |V1, V4; liveness B
|_write answered once_ (CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_04) |a write is presented at
the engine's tag filter's device port |one meta request, none on `tbre_tl_h`, and one answer,
`AccessAck`, with the meta answer's `d_error` |V1, V4
|===

The shared checker does not yet hold checker 1's _lookup carries valid integrity_
(CHK_TF_LOOKUP_03), so _tag filter checks hold_ misses it on this
instance (open decisions).

'''

=== Core write watch

*Rule:* each clear of the tracked capability is checked at the clear port and the RMW filter
against the touches the model saw in its windows ([TP] Core write watch).

[[watch_part]]
==== The core write watch

Part of the engine model (<<engine_model>>).

*Rule:* a core write touches a capability while it is presented on `cored_tl_d`, and from its
acceptance until its answer, at capability granularity ([ToO] Revocation Engine: "every write the
core presents on `cored_tl_d`, and every write it accepted there until the write is answered").

[cols="1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Cycle |What happens

|1 |The engine presents W0's read of the capability on its read port: the watch window starts.
|2 |W0's `Get` leaves on `tbre_tl_h` a cycle later: the TRVK filter or the socket held it. A window
started at `tbre_tl_h` would judge a write in cycle 1 wrongly.
|4 |Write A touches the capability in its watch window: the engine must present no clear.
|6 |The engine presents the clear on its clear port: the watch window ends, the stale window
starts.
|7 |The socket takes the clear; it waits on arbiter input 1. Write B touches the capability in its
stale window: the clear must reach the RMW filter as a read.
|9 |The arbiter passes input 1: the clear reaches the RMW filter and is held there.
|10 |Write C touches the capability while the clear is held: the clear stays as it is, and the
core's tag write reaches the RMW filter after it.
|===

Writes A, B and C are three separate cases, one per window, as in the testplan; the tool tries
every timing.

* *The core's requests:* the model keeps the accepted, unanswered ones in order, at most two
  (assumption A2), each with its capability and whether it is a write. An answer frees the oldest
  (contract C6). The presented request counts too.
* *A write counts until its answer is taken, that cycle included:* a DV reading of "until the write
  is answered".
* *The cycle the clear reaches the RMW filter counts as held, not stale*: [ToO] "Once the
  clear is at the RMW filter, the socket ... holds it there".

'''

[[uw_tbre_watch]]
==== tbre_watch: a capability the core writes keeps its tag

Testplan. A touch in the watch window means no clear; a touch in the
stale window turns the clear into a read at the RMW filter; a held clear stays unchanged.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Run

|_clear only if untouched_ (CHK_TBRE_WATCH_01) |the tracked
capability's clear is presented on the clear port |no touch of it in its watch window |V1, V4
|_stale clear becomes read_ (CHK_TBRE_WATCH_02) |its clear reaches
the RMW filter after a touch in its stale window |the request at the RMW filter is a `Get` of the
same word and bit |V1, V4
|_fresh clear stays write_ (CHK_TBRE_WATCH_03) |its clear reaches
the RMW filter with no touch in its stale window |the request at the RMW filter is the arbiter's
write of tag 0, unchanged |V1, V4
|_clear held unchanged_ (CHK_TBRE_WATCH_04) |any clear is at the RMW
filter and not taken |in the next cycle it is still presented, every field the same, before and
after the squash |V1, V4
|===

'''

[[checks_errors]]
=== Errors, alerts and contracts

*Rule:* checker 3 also checks the engine's error causes, its part of the alert, the contracts the
other checkers assume from it, TL-UL on its ports, and that its own rules can be met ([TP] Errors;
[TP] Subsystem-wide).

[[causes_part]]
==== Error causes

Part of the engine model (<<engine_model>>).

*Rule:* the model flags each engine cause of [ToO] Error Handling in the cycle it occurs, and
remembers that one occurred in this sweep and, for the alert, since reset. An answer counts in the
cycle it is taken.

[cols="4,2,3",options="header"]
|===
|Cause, where the model sees it |`sweep_err` |Alert from the engine

|`d_error` on an answer on `tbre_tl_h` |yes |no
|a broken integrity on an answer on `tbre_tl_h`; in run V3 a malformed one |yes |yes
|`d_error` on a meta answer to the engine's tag filter, at arbiter input 1 |yes |no: the RMW
filter raises it (checker 1)
|`d_error`, a broken integrity or (run V3) a malformed answer on the bitmap port |yes |yes
|an RMW filter fault input raised while active |yes |the fault input itself
|===

* *The tag path's errors raise the alert in the RMW filter:* a meta SRAM error on the engine's tag
  read or clear is a device error on the tag path ([ToO] Error Handling). The RMW filter is a
  blackbox here, so its answers and faults are free and unrelated: checker 3 checks `sweep_err` for
  them, and the alert follows from checker 1's `tag_alerts` ([TP] `tbre_errors`).
* *No integrity fault or malformed answer from the RMW filter:* checker 1 proves its answers well
  formed, and a broken meta SRAM integrity raises its own fault, which the RMW filter fault row
  turns into `sweep_err`. So run V3 drops the answer-shape rules on `tbre_tl_h` and the bitmap port
  only.

'''

[[uw_tbre_errors]]
==== tbre_errors: what fails a sweep and what raises the alert

Testplan. A read error keeps the capability and fails the sweep; the
other causes also raise `fatal_fault`; nothing else sets `sweep_err`.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Run

|_read error, no clear_ (CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_01) |`d_error` on the
answer to a read of the tracked capability on `tbre_tl_h` |no clear for it |V1, V4
|_cause sets sweep error_ (CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_02) |any cause of
<<causes_part>> |a `sweep_err` set request, at some point |V1, V3, V4
|_error set next cycle_ (CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_03) |any cause |that set
request by the next cycle |V1, V3, V4
|_bad answer raises fault_ (CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_04) |a broken integrity
or (V3) a malformed answer on `tbre_tl_h`; any failed lookup |one of the engine's fault inputs, at
some point |V1, V3, V4
|_RMW fault raises alert_ (CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_05) |an RMW filter fault
input while active |the alert request in that cycle |V1, V4
|_error only for a cause_ (CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_06) |a `sweep_err` set
request |a cause is owed one: the same credit as `start_err`{empty}'s |V1, V3, V4
|===

property of its own, the eleven ABVIPs ([ABVIP] TL01 to TL13). Asserted: the engine's requests on

allows still happens. Checker 3's cases: _core two outstanding_ (assumption A2), _every mode value_
(A6), _engine read answers in order_ (A12), _core answers in order_ (contract C6), _input 0 meta
request waits_ (C7), _start strobe_, _base address changes_ and _interrupt state rises_ (C20),

=== State and bounds

*Rule:* every flop has the spec rule that needs it, and every bound the properties use has its
source.

[cols="3,2,3",options="header"]
|===
|Bound |Value |Source

|`TBRE_REGWEN` falls after a taken start |the next cycle |[ToO]: "from the cycle after a taken
start"
|`TBRE_EPOCH.active` against `TBRE_REGWEN` |same cycle |[ToO]: "in the same cycle as
`TBRE_REGWEN` is low"
|busy against `TBRE_REGWEN` |one cycle later |[ToO]: "``TBRE_STATUS.busy`` follows one cycle later"
|the epoch count step |the cycle `active` clears |[ToO]: "incremented in the cycle bit 0 clears"
|`INTR_STATE` set request |the cycle the engine stops being active |[ToO]: "When the engine stops
being active, the `tbre_done` interrupt is raised"
|`intr_tbre_done_o` |this cycle or the next |[CIP] Event-type waveform; `REQ_TBRE_31`
|a clear held at the RMW filter |until taken, unchanged |[ToO]: "holds it there"
|`start_err`, `sweep_err` after a cause, in the bounded checks |by the next cycle |DV reading of
[PG] "check it after a start", "check it once a sweep completes"
|the same, in the unbounded checks; the alert after a cause |no bound |the spec gives none
(testplan premise P7)
|anything else |no bound |the checks follow the order of events, not cycle counts
|===

No helper properties. If the sweep's 31-bit counts slow a proof, the order is cut points, then
helpers, then a counter abstraction recorded in the ledger ([TB] Convergence).

=== Jasper setup

*Rule:* Jasper elaborates the whole design once; checker 3's strategy lives in one task,
`revchk`: the chosen run's properties and every assumption, and stopats on the blocks outside
checker 3.

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Setting |Meaning, default

|`RUN` |`V1` (default), `SafeA`, `V3`, `V4`, `LiveA` or `LiveB`: the run (<<runs>>)
|`FILES` |the file list; default `revchk.scr`
|`TIME_LIMIT` |proof limit; default `1h`
|`FRESH` |`1`: ProofMaster and the prove cache off, for a result to report
|`FORMAL_JOBS`, `COV`, `WITH_PROVEN`, `ASSUME_ASSERTS` |shared, from `formal_ibex_cheriot/scripts`
|===

* *Load:* every file with `FPV_ON` and the run's `REVCHK_RUN` define; elaborate `revchk_env` with
  Jasper's automatic covers (`-create_related_covers`); nothing blackboxed. One clock, `clk_i`; reset while
  `rst_ni` is low.
* *Task:* `revchk` copies the checker's and the rules' properties of the run, with their related
  covers. No RTL assumption is copied, so `CoredReqHeld_M` stays out. Run V3 also drops
  `assume_Rsp_Opcode` and `assume_Rsp_Size` of `u_abvip_xbar` and `u_abvip_bitmap`, by name.
* *Cut points*, in `revchk`: the core's tag filter, the RMW filter, the four access checkers, the
  4:1 arbiter and the register file, and the checker's two inputs the tool may set to anything,
  `k` (the tracked capability) and `tf_pick` (the request the tag filter's tracker follows).
* *Epoch:* in runs V1 and V4, `abstract -reset_value {u_dut.tbre_epoch_q} -constant`: an unknown value,
  the same after every reset, with the counter's logic kept.
* *Results:* `results_<run>.txt` and `summary_<run>.txt`. The script never exits Jasper: it fails
  with an `error`, so it is safe in a live session.

=== Lint

* Verilator 5.048 (`--lint-only -Wall`) on `revchk_checker` and `revchk_env_rules`, with and without
  `FPV_ON`, against the OpenTitan packages, the ABVIP and the shared tag filter folder; the FPV top
  elaborates with both binds for each of the six runs, in simulation and formal builds
  (`CHECKER=revocation bash tools/verify.sh`).
* Liveness properties sit inside `ifdef FPV_ON` and `ifndef VERILATOR`: Verilator rejects
  `s_eventually`.
